idiom_name: struct of widget/driver handles + per-surface functions (Unity or Ceedling runner)
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so a page object becomes a struct owning the handles a surface needs (window, widget, table) plus a set of functions named after the services that surface offers; the toolkit or driver is reached only from those functions, and the test file calls them. What replaces the class is the struct-plus-function convention - and where implementations are swapped, a struct of function pointers as the seam - while Unity or Ceedling supplies setUp/tearDown, assertions and the test runner. Any re-resolution of controls after a re-layout must be written by hand, so keep the driver headers out of the test translation unit where possible.
pitfalls: Handles are captured once: after a re-layout, a new window or a re-render the pointers are stale and the next service call acts on freed widget state - re-run the init function or re-query defensively.
There is no encapsulation boundary: any test can reach the raw toolkit handle and bypass the page functions, which recreates the coupling the struct was meant to remove.
C has no destructor for the page: whatever the surface opens (windows, sessions, buffers) is released explicitly by the test or the runner, so suites leak and become order-dependent.
